01.title: Current Waveform Analysis
01.narrative: The synthetic current shows a weak waveform match to the real signal (correlation 0.055). Its average current is 56.23 A, which is 1.63 A higher than the real average of 54.60 A.

02.title: Power And Energy Delivery Analysis
02.narrative: Power bursts remain weak aligned between the two traces (correlation 0.055). The synthetic average power is 1405.84 W, 2.98% higher than the real average. Both cumulative energy curves should rise steadily if the welding process remains active. The synthetic signal finishes at 14056.58 J versus 13651.06 J, so total delivered energy is 2.97% higher than the real case.

03.title: Quantitative Match Metrics
03.narrative: Lower RMS error is better, while current correlation and ACF correlation should stay close to 1. In this run, the strongest agreement is in amplitude match.

04.title: Frequency And Temporal Pattern Analysis
04.narrative: The dominant spectral peak appears near 1.10 Hz for the real signal and 0.10 Hz for the synthetic signal. A small gap here indicates that the main switching and oscillation frequencies are being preserved. The ACF comparison measures how well repeated temporal patterns survive in the synthetic signal. The current ACF correlation is 0.896, which suggests strong preservation of lag-based structure.

05.title: Heat Transfer And Welding Heat Analysis
05.narrative: With efficiency set to 0.80, the synthetic signal produces 2.97% higher than the real effective heat, while total heat losses are 2.97% higher than the real case. Voltage source used for both cases: Constant 25.00 V.

06.title: Material Response Analysis For Mild Steel
06.narrative: For the mild-steel weld volume defined by area 12.00 mm^2 and length 100.00 mm, the synthetic case shows a temperature difference of 2.94% and a heat-sufficiency difference of 2.97% relative to the real case. The effective-heat gap between real and synthetic cases is 2.97%.

07.title: Peak Detection And Peak-Type Classification
07.narrative: The peak detector found 35 real peaks and 36 synthetic peaks. The dominant category is Class 2 for the real signal and Class 1 for the synthetic signal. Average detected peak power is 1543.42 W for the real data and 1361.79 W for the synthetic data.
